# KineMech

> KineMech is a free, open-source planar mechanism simulator that runs in the browser at https://kinemech.app/. It handles general planar mechanisms of any topology, not only the textbook four-bar and slider-crank: multi-loop linkages and six-bars, gear trains, pin-in-slot joints, and cam-follower pairs. For any of them it computes kinematics, joint forces (kinetostatics), and forward dynamics, the motion a mechanism makes under applied torques and loads. It also synthesizes linkages and designs cam profiles. Version 4.0.0, MIT license, by Tareq Zobaer.

KineMech has three tools that hand designs to each other: the Analyzer (kinematics, forces and dynamics simulation), the Synthesizer (linkage synthesis) and the Profiler (cam design).

## What it does

- Mechanisms: any planar mechanism built from pin, slider, slot, gear and cam joints, with binary, ternary and higher-order links and any number of loops. Examples include four-bars, slider-cranks, Whitworth and shaper quick-return mechanisms, a five-cylinder radial engine, a Stephenson six-bar, the Jansen walking linkage, geared linkages, plate cams, conjugate cams, and one cam driving followers of different types.
- Kinematics: position, velocity and acceleration of every joint and link, including Coriolis terms, by Newton-Raphson on the general constraint equations. Velocity and acceleration polygons, degrees-of-freedom checks, dead-point and change-point detection, Grashof classification and transmission angle.
- Forces (kinetostatics): joint reactions and the input torque or force a prescribed motion needs, with mass and inertia, gravity, point loads, torques, linear and torsional springs and dampers, cam contact force and follower jump, gear mesh force, shaking force and moment, free-body diagrams, and crank counterweight balancing.
- Dynamics (forward dynamics simulation): apply a torque or force to the input (constant, a DC motor line, a speed controller, or a table over time or input angle) and simulate the motion it gives, with fixed-step or adaptive integration. Loads can follow tables over time or crank angle. Every run reports kinetic and potential energy with an energy balance, stops at a follower jump, a change point or an input limit, or carries on through input limits. A flywheel can be sized from the constant-speed cycle and its speed fluctuation checked in a simulation.
- Synthesis: four-bar motion generation (two to four positions), path generation (precision points, or fitting a whole target curve), function generation (Freudenstein, three to five points), quick-return mechanisms, and single- and double-dwell six-bars, with Grashof, transmission-angle and defect checks.
- Cam design: plate, cylindrical and linear cams from rise-dwell-fall programs in eight motion laws, knife-edge, roller, flat-face and spherical followers, pressure angle and undercut checks, and the graphical construction drawn out.
- Units: masses in kg, inertias in kg·m², forces in N, with a physical length unit (m, cm, mm, in, ft) so drawings at any scale give real forces.
- Output: plots against crank angle or time, CSV, animated GIF, and `.kinemech`, `.kinepath` and `.kinemotion` files.
